summary: Describes a way to signal one-click behavior for the List-Unsubscribe email header, because mail software sometimes fetches URLs in headers and would otherwise unsubscribe people by accident.

eli5.summary: Some mail programs peek at links and accidentally press unsubscribe. This adds a signal so only a real button press counts.

questions: why does one-click unsubscribe require dkim
subtitle: A signed email header that tells mail systems they can unsubscribe a user with one automatic HTTPS POST.

tldr.problem: Anti-spam software often fetches URLs in mail headers automatically, so a plain unsubscribe link can trigger accidental unsubscriptions. Confirmation pages protect against that, but they make unsubscribing hard for automated systems.
tldr.mechanism: The sender adds a List-Unsubscribe-Post header with the fixed value List-Unsubscribe=One-Click. A receiver, with user consent, sends that pair in an HTTPS POST to the HTTPS URI in List-Unsubscribe. The message must carry a DKIM signature covering both headers.
tldr.outcome: Senders can tell a deliberate one-click request from an automatic fetch, and receivers can unsubscribe users in the background without parsing a confirmation page.

today: RFC 8058 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It does not update RFC 2369, so ordinary List-Unsubscribe use is unchanged.

sections.title: The Accidental Unsubscribe Problem
sections.content:
A List-Unsubscribe header field (RFC 2369) can hold HTTPS URIs meant to unsubscribe the recipient. But anti-spam software often fetches resources in mail headers without any action by the user, and a sender cannot mechanically tell an automatic fetch from a manual request.

To avoid accidents, senders return landing pages with a confirmation step. A person recognizes it, an automated system does not, so unsubscribing becomes more than one click.

Mailers care about deliverability and want unsubscribing to be easy, because a recipient who finds it hard may report the mail as junk instead. Recipient systems know users do not clearly separate unsubscribing from reporting junk. When an unsubscribe is combined with a junk report, or a system removes closed or abandoned mailboxes, nobody is there to click a confirmation page.
sections.eli5: If a robot tries every link in your mail, it might press "stop sending me this" for you. A confirmation page stops that, but then a robot can never press it on purpose.

sections.title: Goals and the Basic Idea
sections.content:
The RFC adds an HTTPS POST action for mail receivers. Senders can tell it apart from other unsubscribe requests and handle it as a one-click unsubscription with no manual step.

It has two goals: let senders signal that a List-Unsubscribe header has one-click functionality, and let users of a Mail User Agent (MUA) unsubscribe in a familiar place without leaving it. The receiving system can process the request in the background, knowing the sender's system can fully handle it.

The document does not update RFC 2369, so List-Unsubscribe URIs used any other way work as before.
sections.eli5: The mail program sends one small, special message to the sender's website, and the website knows exactly what to do.

sections.title: What Mail Senders Must Do
sections.content:
A sender places one List-Unsubscribe header and one List-Unsubscribe-Post header in the message. The first MUST contain one HTTPS URI and MAY contain other non-HTTP/S URIs such as MAILTO:. The second MUST contain the single pair List-Unsubscribe=One-Click.

Because there is no provision for extra POST arguments, the URI MUST carry enough to identify the recipient and the list. It SHOULD include an opaque or hard-to-forge component, and the server SHOULD verify it. This deters attackers who send spam with unsubscribe links for a victim list, or who POST directly to the unsubscription server.

The POST request MUST NOT include cookies, HTTP authorization or other context, since unsubscribing is unrelated to earlier web activity. The sender MUST NOT return an HTTPS redirect, because redirected POSTs have historically not worked reliably and many browsers turned them into GETs.
sections.eli5: The sender puts a secret-code link in each email. The link has to say who you are and which list, because the special message carries nothing else.

sections.title: What Mail Receivers Do
sections.content:
A receiver does a one-click unsubscription by sending an HTTPS POST to the HTTPS URI in List-Unsubscribe, with the key/value pair from List-Unsubscribe-Post as the request body.

The body SHOULD be sent as multipart/form-data (RFC 7578) and MAY be sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded. These are the encodings browsers use for forms, and the target is the same as for a manual GET unsubscription, so the same server code can handle both.

The receiver MUST NOT POST without user consent. How and when consent is obtained is outside this specification.
sections.eli5: The mail program only presses the button after you say it is okay, and it presses it the same way a web form would.

sections.title: The DKIM Requirement
sections.content:
The message needs at least one valid authentication identifier. In this version only DKIM (RFC 6376) is supported, so senders MUST apply at least one valid DKIM signature.

The List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers MUST be covered by the signature and listed in the h= tag of a valid DKIM-Signature header. If the signature is missing, the receiver SHOULD NOT offer one-click unsubscribe for that message.
sections.eli5: The sender signs the letter so the mail program can tell the unsubscribe link really came from the sender and was not swapped.

sections.title: Header Syntax and IANA Entry
sections.content:
The new header is defined in ABNF, importing fields, WSP and CRLF from RFC 5322. Its only legal argument is List-Unsubscribe=One-Click.

IANA added List-Unsubscribe-Post to the "Permanent Message Header Field Names" registry, with applicable protocol mail, status standard and the IETF as change controller.
sections.eli5: The rules for writing the new header are very strict: there is only one allowed sentence.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The unsubscribe header can include the recipient address, but it is usually also in the To: header. The specification lets anyone with access to a message unsubscribe its recipient, which the RFC notes is typically already true of List-Unsubscribe, just with more steps.

A malicious mailer could try to provoke many unsubscriptions with crafted headers. The RFC judges this unlikely to add much annoyance, since provoking GET requests has long been possible and is easier. The header content is limited to one known key/value pair so an attacker cannot make a POST that simulates a user filling in an arbitrary form on a victim site.

An unsubscribe tells the mailer the address was valid, but the RFC notes simpler ways exist, such as image links. The URI should hold an opaque identifier, and the request carries no cookies, so the server cannot link it to earlier requests.
sections.eli5: The only message allowed is one fixed sentence, so a trickster cannot use it to make your mail program fill in some other website's forms.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives three examples. The simplest has a single HTTPS URI in List-Unsubscribe, and the resulting POST sends List-Unsubscribe=One-Click as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with a Content-Length of 26.

A second example has both a mailto: URI and an HTTPS URI with an opaque query value. The third shows the same pair sent as multipart/form-data with a form boundary, where the form field is named List-Unsubscribe and its content is One-Click.
sections.eli5: The examples show a real header and the exact little message that gets sent back when the button is pressed.

data.title: Header and resulting POST
data.code:
List-Unsubscribe: <https://example.com/unsubscribe/opaquepart>
List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click

POST /unsubscribe/opaquepart HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 26

List-Unsubscribe=One-Click

data.title: List-Unsubscribe-Post
data.code:
fields =/ list-unsubscribe-post

list-unsubscribe-post = "List-Unsubscribe-Post:" 0*1WSP postarg CRLF

postarg = "List-Unsubscribe=One-Click"
